what: evidence that the receipt face has been mounted in a real, non-headless window -- not only in the headless renderer tools/shoot.mjs and tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs drive
why: req/02 W15 clause 3: a face must carry proof of having mounted in a real window a person could look at. tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs and tools/real-window-smoke.mjs in this same faces/receipt/tools/ directory were written from zero for this face, following the same shape faces/ledger, faces/notice and faces/held already established (fixture served over http + shell/tools/real_window.ps1, the shell's own real-window instrument, reused rather than duplicated) -- not by opening any of those faces' own tool files beyond the pattern already documented in req/99.
how: tools/real-window-smoke.mjs starts a static file server rooted at the repo (answering /s-common/tokens.css from the one stylesheet of record -- now tokens/tokens.css, in-repo, per this lane's own tokens-self-ownership atom), then shells out to shell/tools/real_window.ps1 with the fixture's URL. That script opens Chrome in app mode at 1440x900, waits, reads the window's own title back through the Win32 window list, and screenshots the on-screen window rectangle. This face's mount fixture (fixtures/browser-mount-entry.mjs + fixtures/browser-mount.html) imports index.mjs directly, sets data-receipt-id='t-201' on the host, and calls mount(host, stubPort, []) against one delta and its matching receipt spelled out inline in the fixture; the entry script writes the element/section counts into document.title so the numbers below are the numbers the page itself computed, not typed by hand.
colour_status: RESOLVED, not an open gap for this face. This lane found and fixed two independent defects in the shared tokens infrastructure: (1) the stylesheet-of-record pointer (parts/tools/token-source.mjs's TOKEN_SOURCE_RELATIVE, shell/tools/serve.mjs's TOKENS_DEFAULT) pointed at the retired TraceFold_App/ui_proto tree -- replaced with an in-repo, from-zero tokens/tokens.css (req/03 SS635); (2) a genuine CSS parse bug this lane discovered while verifying the fix: the new stylesheet's own header comment contained the literal substring 'faces/*/' in prose, which is also the CSS comment-close token ('*/'), silently truncating the whole stylesheet to zero parsed rules in every renderer (Chrome does not error on this -- it just drops everything after the accidental close). Fixed by rewording the prose. Both real-window captures below show the actual derived palette (light #F6F5F2/#1D1D1D, dark #0A0A0C/#E8E8E8), confirmed against getComputedStyle in a standalone check before this record was written -- see the F-3 lane's own report for the full before/after trail.
